brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Something to keep sewing supplies tidy (a storage organizer with separated spaces for small items)
requirements.evidence: Two adjacent full hex bases (piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0) with a 3-compartment full-depth bin (bin:0,0,0 hex-bin-full-div3) and a 2-compartment full-depth bin (bin:1,0,0 hex-bin-full-div2). Open faces are capped and joints locked; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a small two-cell sewing organizer: two hex bases with one 3-compartment bin and one 2-compartment bin, giving five separated compartments for notions like pins, bobbins, buttons and tape. Exposed faces are capped and joints locked; the build checks clear. I tried to add desk props (pencil, ruler, marker) to the compartments, but they don't fit inside the bins, so none were placed. The build contains no props. I have not verified the bin sizes against your specific supplies.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
